title: Darryl Patterson makes useful things using AI
description: Thirty-five years of designing and building for the web, now pointed at the problems worth solving. Track Tutor, Algoma Live, and where I stand on AI.

hero.headline: Darryl makes useful things using AI.
hero.lead: Thirty-five years of designing and building for the web, now pointed at the problems worth solving.

now.heading: What I do now
paragraphs: I started coding in grade six on a Commodore PET and got onto the web in 1993. Since then I have been the information architect, the UX designer, the back-end and front-end developer, the sysadmin, the department head and the college teacher.

Recently, I've discovered that I have a very particular set of skills. Skills I have acquired over a very long career. Skills that make me very good at using AI to build things that would never have been built otherwise.

built.heading: Two things I built... so far
built.note: Both were designed, built, tested and shipped by me, working with AI coding agents, alongside a day job.

stance.heading: Where I stand on AI
stance.quote: AI should mostly be used for useful things, not just the frivolous.
stance.paragraph: AI is a very divisive topic. It can truly be a source of so much good, resulting in things like earlier health diagnoses and better climate modelling. But it comes at a cost - sustaining AI needs a lot of power and a lot of cooling. And so much of this is being driven by profit, which inevitably leads to the rampant frivolous use of AI. Giving people a fun easy way to create memes and silly songs so they can be kept engaged and captive to advertising seems like a waste of resources. I believe that AI is both an existential threat to humanity and a path to humanity reaching its full potential. I think it's pretty cool that we get to pick the threat or the potential, simply by choosing how we use and interact with AI.

person.heading: The person
person.paragraph: Born and raised in the Sault. 30 years in Toronto building a career and raising a family. Ten years teaching tech at Centennial College. Sailor, singer, Rotarian, father, sound guy. I like making useful things.

cta.heading: Have a problem worth solving?
cta.text: Tell me about it. If I can help, I will. If I can't, I'll help you find someone who can.
